briefing.headline: Midterms reshape US Congress, Welsh devolution debates tech and housing
briefing.overview: US midterm elections have handed Democrats control of Congress and sparked calls for investigations into former President Trump. In Wales, a legal defeat over a leisure centre and a controversial data‑centre proposal highlight tensions in devolved governance.

stories.title: Democrats take Congress, promise probes into Trump
stories.what_happened: Democrats won a majority in the House and Senate in the 2026 midterms. They pledged to launch investigations into alleged corruption linked to former President Trump.
stories.why_it_matters: The shift illustrates how electoral outcomes can alter the balance of power in the US legislature, a key A‑level topic on Congress and party politics. It also raises questions about accountability mechanisms in a presidential system.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Democrats say investigations are needed to protect democratic integrity.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Republicans claim the probes are partisan revenge.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives warn that endless inquiries could destabilise governance.

key_term.definition: When one party holds more than half the seats in a legislative chamber.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how election results can change legislative control in an essay on the US Congress and party competition.

stories.title: Midterm races still undecided
stories.what_happened: Several Senate and House contests remained too close to call after the midterms. Analysts highlighted key battleground states where outcomes could shift the final balance.
stories.why_it_matters: Undecided races demonstrate the role of marginal constituencies and the impact of voter turnout, linking to A‑level study of elections and the first‑past‑the‑post system.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Close races show a healthy, competitive democracy.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: They expose vulnerabilities to strategic voting and misinformation.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives stress the need for electoral reform to better reflect voter intent.

key_term.definition: A constituency where the winning party's majority is small enough that it could easily change in the next election.

stories.exam_use: Cite when discussing the significance of swing seats in US elections essays.

stories.title: Legal challenge to leisure centre closure fails
stories.what_happened: A judge dismissed a legal challenge against the closure of a local leisure centre in Caerphilly. The court upheld the council's decision.
stories.why_it_matters: The case illustrates judicial review of local government actions, a core concept in the A‑level study of the UK judiciary and devolution.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: The decision respects local authority autonomy.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents say it undermines community services.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive groups view it as evidence of austerity pressures on public amenities.

key_term.definition: A process by which courts examine the lawfulness of decisions or actions taken by public bodies.

stories.exam_use: Use as a case study of how courts can check devolved administrations in an essay on the UK judiciary.

stories.title: Welsh MP urged to rethink data‑centre support
stories.what_happened: A campaign group called on former Welsh Secretary Jo Stevens to withdraw her backing for a controversial data‑centre project in her constituency. The group cited environmental concerns.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode highlights intra‑party pressure and the influence of interest groups on policy decisions, linking to A‑level topics on political parties and pressure groups.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say the data centre will bring jobs and investment.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Environmentalists warn of ecological damage and carbon emissions.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives stress economic growth over environmental regulation.

key_term.definition: An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without seeking electoral office.

stories.exam_use: Reference when analysing how pressure groups affect party policy in a UK politics essay.

stories.title: Trump orders Oval Office to become national monument
stories.what_happened: President Trump signed an executive order designating the Oval Office as a national monument after altering its decor. The move follows his recent changes to White House interiors.
stories.why_it_matters: The order shows the use of presidential powers to shape national heritage, relevant to A‑level study of the US executive and its constitutional limits.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents view it as politicising heritage for personal legacy.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives argue it distracts from pressing policy issues.

key_term.definition: A directive issued by the US President that manages operations of the federal government.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate executive authority in an essay on the US presidency.

compare.uk: The UK Prime Minister leads the executive, accountable to Parliament and can be removed by a vote of no confidence.
compare.us: The US President heads the executive, elected separately from Congress and cannot be removed except by impeachment.
compare.insight: The contrast shows how the UK’s fused executive‑legislature system allows quicker removal of leaders, while the US’s separation creates a more stable but less flexible executive.

ideas_lens.text: Trump’s monument order reflects a conservative emphasis on preserving traditional symbols and national heritage, echoing Edmund Burke’s idea that institutions embody collective memory.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which the US President can use executive orders to shape national policy, using recent examples.
exam_question.tip: Analyse the legal basis, political context and potential challenges of each order.
